summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old female was admitted with worsening lower extremity edema and severe fatigue. The swelling was multifactorial, due to chronic venous insufficiency, lymphedema, obesity, and recent dose increase of nifedipine, which was held. Vancomycin was started for suspected cellulitis but discontinued due to lack of infection signs. Increased diuresis with lasix and metolazone led to acute kidney injury, so these were stopped. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.4, prompting warfarin adjustment and a dose of Lovenox, later held due to renal concerns. Phenytoin was held due to elevated levels from impaired kidney function. Fatigue was attributed to untreated obstructive sleep apnea, supported by hypercarbia on ABG; a sleep clinic appointment was scheduled. She was discharged home with compression stockings, instructions to elevate legs, and plans for outpatient follow-up, including INR and creatinine monitoring, sleep study, and physical therapy.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Need for prophylactic vaccination and inoculation against influenza
